text:
eli: Heads-up — after flipping the FA v3 kernel by default in the canary pool we see a consistent ~8-12% p95 tail increase on mixed-GPU nodes. Dumped a few traces, looks like workspace churn + a handful of allocator stalls. anyone else? :eyes:
mei: saw something similar on my perfCI runs yesterday. Were the workspace shapes identical vs the v2 runs? small-batch, long-seq workloads?
arjun: we changed scheduler affinity rules in the kernel-selection RFC (bind-heavy -> bin-pack with affinity) — could be causing multiple concurrent workspaces to be placed on the same GPU and fragment the allocator. can you share the autobench commands you used?
eli: ran ./tools/autobench --model gpt-j-6b --seq 1024 --batch 2 --flash v2 then v3, same harness otherwise. raw: v2 p95=74ms, v3 p95=82ms, avg token cost similar. attached logs: alloc stalls show repeated fast alloc/free patterns.
mei: that matches a KV-cache miss/regrowth pattern we saw before — if a kernel chooses a larger workspace layout it can push other contexts to reallocate, hitting allocator slowpaths and cudaFree-sync.
jess: deploy-bot: canary roll applied to pool-canary-03 (tag=fa-v3-canary) :white_check_mark:
arjun: quick telemetry query that helped me isolate this earlier: ```promql
sum(rate(runtime_alloc_latency_ms_bucket{kernel=~"flashattn.*"}[5m])) by (le, kernel)
``` shows a second modal bucket after v3 flip. also look at metric `workspace_frag_percent` per GPU.
eli: good call. I also added traces: `runtime.trace.alloc_free` shows 3x more small frees during the window.
mei: two hypotheses: 1) v3 chooses tiling that uses more ephemeral workspace (higher peak but fewer kernels), which thrashes our small-block allocator; 2) scheduler affinity puts heterogeneous seq shapes together making per-GPU max-residency higher, causing spills and extra copies.
arjun: tests to run: A) homogeneous GPUs (one instance type) with v2/v3 -- if delta disappears, scheduler+packing likely root. B) force kernel selector to prefer smaller workspaces (simulate an opt-in hint) and rerun. C) run with `ALLOW_WORKSPACE_COMPACTION=false` to see impact (we saw previously it reduces latency variance).
eli: I pushed a quick local runtime toggle patch: ```
// runtime/config.cc
"kernel_selector": { "prefer_small_workspace": true }
``` applied to a local daemon — p95 dropped back ~5% vs v3-default but still slightly above v2.
jess: can we add a short-lived telemetry tag to identify affected requests? maybe `kernel_choice_override=true` so we can filter logs without long retention.
arjun: will add `kernel_choice_reason` label (auto|hint|fallback) to the kernel telemetry. also adding per-gpu `workspace_resident_count` gauge so we can spot overpacking.
mei: for an autobench job I recommend this invocation (covers mix-heavy cases): ```bash
./tools/autobench --model llama-2-13b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --flash v3 --mix "short:70,med:20,long:10" --reps 200
``` gather p50/p90/p95 and `workspace_frag_percent` per-gpu.
eli: running that now on canary-03. will post results. if we confirm scheduler packing is the culprit, we can either relax affinity or add a packing-aware cost function that penalizes high workspace residency.
jess: for rollout safety, suggest a circuit-breaker: if cluster-wide workspace_frag_percent > 0.25 && p95 increase > 7% then auto-fallback to v2 for that pool. ops-bot can wire it into the route policies.
arjun: agree. I'll prototype a simple scoring tweak: score += residency_penalty * projected_workspace if projected_workspace > threshold. low-risk change and revertable.
eli: results in — mix run: v2 p95=120ms, v3-default p95=133ms, v3+prefer_small_workspace p95=126ms. workspace_frag_percent averaged 0.31 on mixed nodes, 0.12 on homogeneous.
mei: that strongly points to packing + workspace choice interaction. thanks for the numbers.
jess: creating a short RFC follow-up to propose a scheduler cost-term + telemetry labels and the circuit-breaker policy. I'll drop a stub in #eng-runtime and reference this thread.
arjun: plan: (1) add labels + workspace_resident_count telemetry (2) roll scoring tweak as canary (3) add circuit-breaker rule to console for canary pools (4) run autobench matrix across gpu types. estimated 3-4 sprints to full rollout.
eli: sounds good. small ask — can we get a quick postmortem blurb for PMs noting tradeoff: v3 reduced compute kernel runtime in many cases but increases alloc churn on mixed-packing workloads; scheduler/co-location needs to be packing-aware.
mei: +1. will help craft language.
eli: thanks all. will leave logs in /tmp/fa_v3_canary_dump.tar.gz and ping when the autobench finishes. :thumbsup:
